methods.name: Split at the x-intercepts
methods.summary: Find the roots, integrate over each section separately, and add the absolute values.

methods.name: Negate the part below the axis
methods.summary: For a region entirely below the axis, use −∫ f(x) dx to get a positive area.

methods.name: Integrate |f| on the GDC
methods.summary: On P2, compute ∫ |f(x)| dx in one step.

methods.name: Use symmetry
methods.summary: Use matching pieces, e.g. sin x on [0, 2π] has two congruent humps, so the area is 2 × ∫ from 0 to π of sin x dx.

misconceptions: Integrating straight across a root so the positive and negative parts cancel
Giving a negative number as an area
Splitting at a turning point instead of at the x-intercept

threads.echo: A definite integral adds signed pieces, like displacement; an area, like distance, needs every piece counted as positive.
The two humps of sin x over a full period are congruent, so one integral doubled gives the area, just as the unit circle's symmetry relates angles.

skills.name: Find the area between two curves (or a curve and a line)
examTypes: Find the area of the region enclosed by y = x² and y = 2x + 3
Write down an integral expression for the area between the two curves
The curves intersect at A and B. Find the area of the region enclosed between them

methods.name: Integrate top minus bottom
methods.summary: Find the intersections, then integrate (upper curve − lower curve) between them.

methods.name: Split where the curves cross
methods.summary: If the curves swap over, split at each intersection and use (upper − lower) on each piece.

methods.name: GDC with |f − g|
methods.summary: Find the intersections on the GDC, then evaluate ∫ |f(x) − g(x)| dx between them.

methods.name: Area under the top minus area under the bottom
methods.summary: Find each area under its curve separately and subtract, e.g. a trapezium under the line minus the area under the parabola.

misconceptions: Integrating lower − upper and reporting a negative area
Using the x-intercepts of one curve as limits instead of the intersection points
Not splitting where the curves cross, so the pieces cancel

threads.echo: The limits are where the curves meet: solve f(x) = g(x) by algebra or with the GDC intersect tool, exactly as in SL2.10.
Each thin strip has height (top − bottom) and width dx; adding all the strips gives the area.

skills.name: Find an unknown limit or parameter from a given integral or area
examTypes: Given ∫ from 1 to k of (2x + 1) dx = 10, find k
The area of the region enclosed by y = kx², the x-axis and x = 3 is 18. Find k
Find the value of a, 0 < a < π/2, such that ∫ from 0 to a of cos x dx = 0.5

methods.name: Integrate, then solve for the unknown
methods.summary: Evaluate the integral in terms of the unknown, set it equal to the given value and solve (often a quadratic in k).

methods.name: Solve on the GDC
methods.summary: Graph the integral as a function of the unknown against a horizontal line at the target value, or use the solver.

methods.name: Scale a known area
methods.summary: If the parameter is a vertical stretch (y = kx²), the area scales by k, so find the area for k = 1 and divide.

misconceptions: Keeping a root for the upper limit that is below the lower limit or outside the given range
Forgetting to subtract F(lower) when it is not zero
Treating k as the variable of integration

threads.echo: F(k) = 10 is where the graph of y = F(k) meets a horizontal line, so factorising and the GDC must give the same k.

skills.name: Find the area of a region bounded by a curve, a tangent or normal, and an axis
examTypes: The tangent at P meets the x-axis at Q. Find the area of the region bounded by the curve, the tangent and the x-axis
Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve, the normal at A and the y-axis
Show that the area of R is 9/4

methods.name: Integral plus or minus a triangle
methods.summary: Split the region into a part under the curve (an integral) and a triangle under the line, then add or subtract.

methods.name: Top minus bottom, piece by piece
methods.summary: Integrate (upper boundary − lower boundary) over each x-interval, changing the formula where the boundary changes.

methods.name: GDC for the pieces
methods.summary: Find the key intersection points on the GDC and evaluate each integral numerically.

misconceptions: Using the curve's x-intercept as the end of the triangle instead of the tangent's
Adding a piece that should be subtracted, counting the region under the line twice
Forgetting that the lower boundary changes at the point of contact

threads.echo: Every corner of the region is an intersection of two graphs (curve, line or axis), found by solving or by GDC.
